sa_market_summary: The Toyota Starlet is a rebadged, Indian-built Suzuki Baleno and one of South Africa's ten best-selling used cars: AutoTrader recorded 595 used Starlet sales in September 2026 at an average of R228,622 and 38,269km. The 2020-2022 cars use a 1.4-litre K14B engine (68kW), while the 2023 facelift moved to a 1.5-litre K15B (77kW), both with a 5-speed manual or a dated 4-speed automatic. It offers Toyota's dealer network and resale value at a budget price, but buyers should check safety specification closely: Global NCAP gave the pre-update car a zero-star adult occupant rating because it had only two airbags, and the AA reports that six airbags became standard only from September 2025.

known_faults.description: The 1.4-litre K14B engine is reported to suffer carbon build-up and pre-ignition, which shows as knocking under load, hesitation and reduced economy. Running on lower-octane fuel makes it worse; 95 octane is recommended.
known_faults.what_to_inspect: Listen for pinging or knocking when accelerating uphill in a high gear. Ask which fuel the owner used and check for stored knock-sensor or misfire codes.
known_faults.source: AutoTrader SA Toyota Starlet Buyer's Guide

known_faults.fault: Rough idle from blocked idle control valve
known_faults.description: Some 1.4 Starlets develop an unsteady or hunting idle when the idle control valve and throttle body become clogged.
known_faults.what_to_inspect: Let the engine idle with the air conditioning on and off. The rev needle should stay steady with no stumbling.
known_faults.source: AutoTrader SA Toyota Starlet Buyer's Guide

known_faults.fault: Sensor faults and warning lights (1.5 K15B)
known_faults.description: The newer 1.5-litre K15B has limited long-term local data, but occasional sensor faults that trigger dashboard warning lights have been reported.
known_faults.what_to_inspect: Confirm no warning lights stay on after start-up and request a diagnostic scan for stored codes.
known_faults.estimated_repair_zar: R1,000 - R4,000 (sensor replacement, usually under warranty)
known_faults.source: AutoTrader SA Toyota Starlet Buyer's Guide

known_faults.fault: Uneven front tyre wear and suspension creaks
known_faults.description: Front tyres can wear unevenly when wheel alignment is neglected, and worn bushings or shocks cause creaking over rough SA roads and speed bumps.
known_faults.what_to_inspect: Check the inner edges of the front tyres for feathering. Drive over speed bumps and listen for creaks or knocks from the front suspension.
known_faults.source: AutoTrader SA Toyota Starlet Buyer's Guide

what_to_inspect_before_buying: Check the airbag count: pre-September 2025 cars have two airbags and scored zero stars for adult protection in Global NCAP testing
Confirm whether it is a 1.4 (2020-2022) or 1.5 (2023+) car, as the 1.5 is stronger and more economical
Listen for knocking or pinging under load on 1.4 models and ask which fuel octane was used
Check idle quality with the air conditioning on
Inspect front tyres for uneven wear and test the suspension over bumps
Look for stone chips on the bonnet and front bumper
Verify Toyota service history and remaining warranty or service plan
Test the 4-speed automatic at highway speed if buying an auto, as it feels slow at full load
owner_sentiment: Positive. Owners value the Starlet's low running costs, roomy cabin for its size, Toyota badge, and strong resale value. The main criticisms are the dated 4-speed automatic, the 1.4's modest performance at Highveld altitude, light build quality and, on earlier cars, the two-airbag safety specification.
